question: The circumference of magnetic field lines __________ as we move away from a current carrying a straight conductor.
solution:
The correct answer is __**increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **circumference of magnetic field** lines around a current-carrying conductor increases as the distance from the conductor increases.
 
• This relationship is a direct consequence of the geometrical nature of magnetic field lines forming concentric circles around the conductor.
 
• The magnetic field strength decreases with distance, but the circumference of the field lines grows, following the formula** B ∝ 1/r, **where B is the magnetic field strength and r is the radius.
 
• According to Ampère's circuital law, the integral of the magnetic field around a closed loop is proportional to the electric current passing through the loop.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Field Lines:**

 
 
• Imaginary lines used to represent the strength and direction of a magnetic field.
 
• They form closed loops from the north pole to the south pole of a magnet.
 
 
 
• **Ampère's Circuital Law:**
 
 
• States that the line integral of the magnetic field around a closed loop is equal to the permeability times the electric current enclosed by the loop.
 
• Mathematically represented as ∮B·dl = μ₀Iₑₙₚ.
 
 
 
• **Right-Hand Rule:**
 
 
• A mnemonic is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field relative to the current direction.
 
• Point the thumb in the direction of the current, and the curl of the fingers shows the direction of the magnetic field lines.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field Strength (B):**
 
 
• Measured in teslas (T) or gauss (G), it represents the force exerted by the field on a moving charge.
 
• Depends on the current and the distance from the conductor.
